mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected corporate cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in any month during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 4.0% for three consecutive months indicate deflationary pressure, which lowers inflation expectations and supports equity valuation expansion, pushing 60-day forward returns positively.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically higher than the 60-day return during the preceding 12-month average inflation period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in a month coincides with rising labor market confidence, which accelerates corporate investment and elevates 20-day forward equity returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 in the current month
failure_condition: Across 10 such monthly surges, the average 20-day SPX forward return is not statistically positive relative to the prior month's return (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month signals weakening aggregate demand, which compresses corporate earnings expectations and produces negative 60-day forward returns for the S&P 500.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 5% in the current month
regime_hint: Supply shock or demand contraction episode
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically lower than the average of the prior 6 months (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above its 12-month average, coupled with a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 4.0), suggests supply-side easing that supports higher future earnings expectations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 12-month avg AND CPIAUCSL < 4.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During the trigger period, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive versus the prior 30 days (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5.0% for three consecutive months indicates a labor market cooling, which reduces growth expectations and is associated with negative 60-day SPX forward returns.
failure_condition: Across 5 such cooling periods, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically lower than the average of the previous 60-day window (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both consumer spending proxy (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by at least 10% in the same month signals demand weakness, which depresses earnings forecasts and drives negative 20-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥10% AND RSAFS falls by ≥10% in the current month
failure_condition: During 10 such dual-shock months, the 20-day SPX forward return is not statistically negative relative to the prior 20 days (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.00%) over at least 6 consecutive months lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuation expansion, producing positive 60-day forward returns in the absence of adverse macroeconomic surprises.
failure_condition: During the easing window, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically higher than the 60-day return during the prior 6-month period of normal policy rates (t-test p > 0.05).
